item.title: Mounting an Everpure Cloud Azure Native Snapshot for Recovery on Linux
item.description: Are you looking for a way to get a few files back from an Everpure Cloud Azure Native snapshot without overwriting the live volume? The portal gives you two options today: overwrite the volume group, or restore the snapshot into a brand new volume group. Overwrite is destructive, and a new volume group means a new iSCSI target to mount on the VM. What I usually want is the old copy of one volume mounted next to the current one, so I can copy back what I need and throw the copy away. So I wrote a script that does exactly that. I started with Linux, and in Part 2 I do the same thing on Windows.

item.title: Using CloudFormation to Manage EC2 in AWS
item.description: An update to a topic I previously covered! How can we automate management of virtual machines in AWS? Cloud Formation (CFT) is another way that can accomplish it. This blog will identify how you can create, update and delete a CFT stack to be able to manage your EC2 infrastructure.

item.title: Deploying a Linux EC2 Instance with Hashicorp Terraform and Vault to AWS and Connect to Everpure Cloud Dedicated
item.description: Another update to my “Terraforming AWS” series is the ability to deploy a Linux based Instance and connect to an existing data volume sitting on the Everpure Cloud Dedicated. This post will cover how to setup your environment and deploy and bootstrap your linux instance to connect via ISCSI.
